name: PA-16
label: Likely R

No polls or expert ratings; markets price Kelly at ~95%
model.rationale: Kelly holds a heavily Republican district, a massive fundraising edge, and prediction markets price his reelection around 95%, with no polling or ratings suggesting a competitive race. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin with a slight tightening for the incumbent's incumbency edge.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Wagner within single digits would warrant moving this toward Tossup.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Kelly seeks another term in a northwestern Pennsylvania district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.2 million and holding $1.3 million on hand, while Democrat Justin Wagner has raised under $70,000. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Kelly about a 95 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point firmly to Kelly: the district's partisan lean, his incumbency, and the money gap all favor the Republican, though a modestly favorable national environment for Democrats keeps the expected margin somewhat narrower than the raw lean suggests. Absent unexpected outside spending or late polling movement, this race is unlikely to become competitive.
